instrument_construction: Z = 1 if the district's prior-cycle council race was close (margin_pct <= bandwidth) AND won by a Democrat; 0 if close and won by a Republican; cell excluded from the sample otherwise (sharp-RD exclusion). prior cycle = canonical election_year - 4 (2017/2021/2025 -> 2013/2017/2021).
total_units_exclusion: TOTAL UNITS == RESIDENTIAL UNITS + COMMERCIAL UNITS for 99.6% of canonical rows (verified on this build); dropping it keeps the linear design non-singular. Information-preserving, documented.

model4_benchmark.label: Model 4 — 51 council-district FE, classical SE
model4_benchmark.note: Model 4 pools all districts/years (classical-SE row shown; the clustered-SE counterpart shares the coefficient). The IV sample is restricted to close-race cells, so compare the dem_share coefficient — not the sample size — across designs.

bw_5pp.not_identifiable_reason: design matrix rank-deficient (regressor block 15/16, instrument block 15/16); only 4 close-race cells across 3 districts. Root cause, verified numerically (residual of Z on the FE block is ~1e-11, i.e. exact): Z varies only at the (district, prior-election-cycle) level, and in this canonical dataset election_year is a deterministic grouping of sale_year (2016-18->2017, 2019-23->2021, 2024-25->2025), so every close-race cell is exactly a district x sale-year-window interaction of the district and sale_year fixed effects. With so few close cells the additive district+year FE span ANY cell-level binary instrument, so the first stage has zero residual instrument variation. This is not a choice that can be coded around: NYC has too few close council races for this instrument to be identified under district FE.
bw_5pp.verdict: instrument is weak at this bandwidth — treat as suggestive, not identified

headline.note: Weak instrument (first-stage F <= 10) at a bandwidth means the 2SLS estimate there is suggestive only and biased toward OLS; the close-election design then cannot rescue identification at that bandwidth.
